rationale: The plan chooses the right family of methods for raw Salmon counts with n=3/group — DESeq2 Wald with an explicit control reference level and an edgeR quasi-likelihood cross-check — and correctly refuses to loosen alpha to compensate for low power, stating the expected 20-40% sensitivity ceiling. QC (blind VST PCA, sample distance heatmap, library sizes, explicit flagging rather than silent dropping), a minimal >=10 counts in >=3 samples filter, model-internal median-of-ratios/TMM normalization, BH at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering and a p-value histogram check, and apeglm shrinkage used for ranking while retaining Wald p-values are all stated explicitly and correctly. Enrichment was not requested but is reasonably included as preranked fgsea on the Wald statistic with a 15-500 size window and named collections; it loses a couple of points because it only promises to state versions rather than naming them, and layering three collections adds unnecessary multiplicity for a small study. Minor deductions elsewhere for the unresolved 7-column/6-sample confusion and for presenting the DESeq2-edgeR intersection as the headline 'high-confidence' set, which is a heuristic rather than a calibrated error rate; the reporting step is otherwise complete on design, versions, thresholds, counts at each stage, caveats, and reproducibility.
